title: Fabrication of Gradient Nanopattern by Thermal Nanoimprinting Technique and Screening of the Response of Human Endothelial Colony-forming Cells
protocol: Wear personal protective equipment including nitrile gloves, goggles and lab coat.
Perform electropolishing in a fume hood.
Mix ethyl alcohol (C2H5OH, 99.9%) and perchloric acid (HClO4, 60%) in a 1 L double jacket beaker at a ratio of 4:1.
Connect the double jacket beaker to a circulator and set the temperature to 7 °C.
Leave the electropolishing solution under stirring for at least 30 min until it reaches 7 °C.
Immerse an ultrapure Al plate (99.999%, 20 × 50 × 1 mm³) and a carbon counter electrode into the electropolishing solution using crocodile clips and copper wire.
Adjust the position of the Al plate and the carbon counter electrode to face each other.
Connect the Al plate to the positive terminal, and the carbon counter electrode to the negative terminal, of a DC power supply.
Turn off the magnetic stirrer.
Apply a voltage of 20 V for 4 min.
Turn on the magnetic stirrer and allow it to run for another 6 min.
Turn off the power supply.
Manually separate the Al plate from the clip.
Rigorously wash the Al plate with deionized water.
Dry the Al plate with nitrogen.
Store the Al plate under inert gas.
Load 590 mL of deionized water into a glass bottle.
Add 400 mL of methyl alcohol (CH3OH, 99%) to the glass bottle.
Add 10 mL of phosphoric acid (H3PO4, 85%) to the glass bottle.
Mix the solution well by shaking manually or with magnetic stirring.
Pour 500 mL of electrolyte into a 1 L double jacket beaker.
Immerse the polished Al plate and carbon counter electrode into the solution with crocodile clips and copper wire.
Add additional electrolyte to locate the boundary of electropolishing 2-3 mm above the surface of the solution.
Install a vertical shaft on a U-shape pedestal.
Attach an overhead stirrer and impeller using metal clamps.
Position the propeller of the impeller near the lower end of both electrodes.
Set the rotation speed of the overhead stirrer between 200 and 300 rpm.
Connect the double jacket beaker to a circulator and set the temperature at -10 °C.
Leave the system for at least 1 h under stirring until the temperature drops to -10 °C.
Apply a voltage of 195 V under stirring for 16 h.
Prepare chromic acid etching solution by dissolving 9.0 g of chromium oxide and 20.3 mL of phosphoric acid in 500 mL of deionized water.
Pour the etching solution into the 1 L double jacket beaker.
Set the temperature at 65 °C.
Immerse the anodized Al plate in the etching solution for at least 10 h under stirring.
Seal the top of the beaker with aluminum foil.
Rinse the etched Al plate several times with deionized water.
Set the same experimental conditions as step 2.1.1 to 2.1.7.
Load the etched Al plate to the anode of the system and apply a voltage of 195 V for 6 h.
Turn off the power supply and manually separate the Al plate from the clip.
Immediately wash the anodized Al plate with deionized water.
Prepare a pore widening solution by dissolving 5.765 g of phosphoric acid in 500 mL of deionized water.
Pour the solution into a 1 L double jacket beaker.
Connect the double jacket beaker to the circulator and set the temperature at 30 °C.
Set the moving part of the linear stage to the home position.
Attach the clip to the bracket and load the anodized Al plate.
Manipulate the position of the Al plate so that it will come right above the surface of the solution without touching it.
Start a stopwatch as soon as the Al plate touches the surface of the solution.
Gradually immerse the Al plate into the solution at a speed of 4.86 µm/s for 120 min to make a 35 mm AAO mold with a size gradient from 120 nm to 200 nm (GP 120/200).
Immerse the entire area of GP 120/200 mold in the pore widening solution for 2 h to make a GP 200/280 mold.
Immerse the entire area of GP 120/200 mold in the pore widening solution for 4 h to make a GP 280/360 mold.
Rinse the gradient Al plate several times with deionized water.
Pour 140 mL of sulfuric acid (H2SO4, 95%) into a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) beaker.
Add 60 mL of hydrogen peroxide dropwise (H2O2, 30%).
Leave the mixture for 30 min until it has cooled down.
Immerse the AAO mold in the solution for 30 s using a nonmetallic tweezer.
Rinse the AAO mold several times with deionized water.
Soak the mold in deionized water for 30 min and put it in methyl alcohol for another 30 min.
Dry the AAO mold under vacuum for 3 h.
Fill one-third of a 1 L n-hexane bottle with molecular sieves.
Seal the bottle with paraffin film and store it under dry nitrogen for 24 h.
Filter 200 mL of n-hexane using a glass syringe and 0.2 µm PTFE syringe filter.
Pour 80 mL of filtered n-hexane into a 100 mL glass bottle.
Add 2 mL of HDFS to the mixture.
Load 57 mL of filtered n-hexane in a 100 mL beaker.
Immerse the AAO mold into the solvent containing HDFS.
Wait 10 min for the reaction to proceed.
Transfer the AAO mold to fresh n-hexane.
Close and seal all reagent bottles that contain HDFS.
Soak the AAO mold in 60 mL of methoxynonafluorobutane.
Ultrasonically clean the AAO mold in a beaker for 10 s per time.
Repeat ultrasonic cleaning procedure 10 times to remove physically adsorbed HDFS molecules.
Completely dry the AAO mold under vacuum for 24 h.
Cut a 1.1 mm thick polystyrene sheet to a size of 2.9 mm wide by 3.7 mm long using a printed circuit board (PCB) cutter.
Cut the AAO mold 35 mm from the bottom using a nipper.
Mark the sample name and date of manufacture on the back of the polystyrene sheet.
Clean an 8.0" wafer with a small dose of ethyl alcohol.
Put the polystyrene sheets on the cleaned wafer.
Mount the AAO mold onto the wafer.
Place the bottom film in the drawer of a thermal imprinter.
Attach the top film to the gasket.
Put the wafer on the bottom film.
Place the gasket on the wafer.
Ensure there is no dust on the wafer before proceeding.
Close the drawer of the thermal imprinter.
Apply 165 °C of heat and 620.52 kPa of pressure for 100 s in the thermal imprinter.
Cool the sample to room temperature after heating.
Gently twist the polystyrene sheet to release the AAO mold.
Place the nanopattern plates on a square dish.
Pour 100 mL of 70% ethyl alcohol onto the plates.
Expose the plates to ultraviolet light for 30 min.
Dry the nanopattern plates with nitrogen.
Transfer the nanopattern plates to an oxygen plasma generator.
Evacuate the chamber until it reaches 1.33 Pa.
Inject oxygen at a rate of 30 cm³/min into the evacuated chamber.
Apply a radio frequency power of 60 W in the oxygen plasma generator.
Maintain the oxygen plasma for 90 s.
Attach the nanopattern plate to the bottom of a cell culture dish using a drop of toluene.
Incubate a collagen-coated 12-well culture dish at 37°C for 1 hour.
Wash the 12-well culture dish using 1× sterile phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Collect 50 mL of human blood using a heparin inhibitor tube.
Put 6 mL of hydrophilic polysaccharide solution in a 15 mL tube.
Add 8 mL of blood to the hydrophilic polysaccharide solution.
Centrifuge the tube at 1020 x g for 20 minutes.
Harvest the opaque cell layer and transfer it to a new 15 mL tube.
Add 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS)-contained PBS to the tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 1020 x g for 10 minutes.
Remove the supernatant from the tube.
Add red-blood-cell lysis buffer to the pellet and keep on ice for 5 minutes.
Add 10% FBS-contained PBS to the tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 1020 x g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant from the tube.
Add 1 mL of endothelial cell expansion medium supplemented with 10% FBS.
Seed 8.0 × 10^6 cells per well in each collagen-coated dish.
Change the culture medium every day for one week.
Then, change the culture medium every two days.
Culture hECFCs in endothelial cell expansion medium supplemented with 5% FBS and penicillin/streptavidin at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO2.
Replace the medium once daily.
Grow cells to passage 7 for further experiments.
Coat gradient nanopattern plates with 1 mL of 0.1% protein coating solution in PBS for 10 min at room temperature.
Create a hECFC suspension using trypsin from culture dishes by standard cell-splitting method.
Dilute the hECFC suspension to achieve desired confluence.
Seed hECFCs onto gradient nanopattern plates and flat control (e.g., 1.0 × 104 cells/cm2).
Culture the cells on flat or gradient nanopattern plates for 2 days in the incubator.
Fix hECFCs cultured on flat or gradient nanopattern plates with 2.5% glutaraldehyde at 4 °C overnight.
Treat samples with 1% osmium tetroxide for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash samples with PBS.
Dehydrate samples sequentially in ethyl alcohol from 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, to 100% concentrations for 10 minutes each.
Treat samples with hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS) for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Wash samples again with fresh HMDS and leave them under the fume hood until residual HMDS evaporates completely, typically for at least one day.
Coat the samples with platinum sputter coater for 5 minutes.
Examine the samples with a scanning electron microscope (SEM).
Fix hECFCs cultured on flat or gradient nanopattern plates with a mixture of 2% paraformaldehyde and 2.5% glutaraldehyde in PBS at 4 °C overnight.
Perform post-fixation using 1% osmium tetroxide.
Dehydrate samples sequentially in ethyl alcohol from 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, to 100% concentrations for 10 minutes each.
Embed samples in epoxy resin.
Make 60 nm thick sections from blocks and place them on a TEM grid.
Stain the section with uranyl acetate and lead citrate mixture.
Obtain images with a transmission electron microscope (TEM).
Fix hECFCs cultured on flat or gradient nanopattern plates with 4% paraformaldehyde at room temperature for 15 min.
Permeabilize and block samples with 5% goat serum and 0.1% octylphenol ethoxylate in PBS (PBST) at room temperature for 30 min.
Incubate samples with anti-human vinculin primary antibody (1:500 in PBST) at room temperature for 2 h.
Rinse samples three times with PBST.
Incubate samples with fluorescence-conjugated phalloidin (1:1,000 in PBST), fluorescence-conjugated secondary antibody (1:1,000 in PBST) at room temperature for 2 h.
Rinse samples three times with PBST.
Incubate samples with 4', 6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI, 1:1,000 in PBST) at room temperature for 5 min.
Drop 10 µL of mounting medium on the surface of gradient nanopattern.
Place a coverslip on the mounting medium.
Place the sample upside down on the sample stage and acquire images using confocal fluorescence microscope.
